Shady is a concept AI scam checker built for families, including first-time smartphone users.Shady is a concept AI scam checker built for families, including first-time smartphone users.

Paste any message and get a calm answer (Likely a scam, Not sure or Likely safe) with the red flags underlined in your own words and one clear next step. When it isn't sure, Shady asks someone you trust.

The challenge

Scams win on speed and silence:

  • 57% of adults worldwide met a scam last year
  • 64% of scams are over within a day of first contact
  • 22% of targeted older people told no one because they felt too embarrassed
  • Existing checkers give a score, but people need the why, in their own language, and someone to ask

The approach

Not a score, but an answer with the evidence. Shady gives an honest verdict with its confidence in words, underlines the red flags in the message itself and offers one clear next step. When it is not sure, one tap sends the message to someone you trust, and their reply comes back in the app.

The details

  • Honest, not absolute: always "likely", never "100% safe"
  • Every verdict points to the exact words, links or numbers
  • A "Take a breath" pause, because scammers want you to rush
  • Names, numbers and accounts are blurred before checking
  • Accessible by default: 18px text, 48px targets, 4.5:1 contrast, voice in and out, and verdicts never shown by colour alone
  • One light and dark design system, where every colour is a token

Concept project. Statistics: GASA and Feedzai, Global State of Scams 2025; Age UK.

how it landed

OutcomeOutcome

A concept project. The prototype numbers come from my own tests; the rest are the results it is designed for, not live numbers.

What I delivered

  • Brand, logo and a light and dark design system
  • 16 app screens and 6 web screens
  • A working web-app prototype: 36 of 36 tested flows pass, and 10 of 10 test messages are judged right
  • A 41-second launch film

How I’d measure success

  • Time from pasting a message to knowing what to do
  • How often "Not sure" ends with a reply from family
  • Scams stopped before anyone clicks or pays
  • Whether older users feel calmer, and less embarrassed to ask

What it shows

  • Designing AI people can trust: honest, explainable and easy to correct
  • Accessibility built in from the first screen
  • Taking a product from research to a working prototype
  • Motion used to tell the story
